evidence.note: Logs x_for directly using logger.debug without sanitizing or stripping newlines
_get_real_value parses the header and returns an item from the list without stripping CRLF characters
parse_list_header splits and strips spaces/tabs but preserves newline/carriage return characters within header values

arguments.suggested_fix: Sanitize `x_for` (e.g. by stripping or replacing newline characters) or log it safely (or via representation/quoting) before passing it to `_logger.debug`.
arguments.explanation: The new debug logging statement in ProxyFix logs the value of `x_for` (derived from the `X-Forwarded-For` HTTP header via `_get_real_value` and `parse_list_header`) directly using standard logging (`_logger.debug`). Since `parse_list_header` does not strip newline or carriage return characters from header values, an attacker can supply an `X-Forwarded-For` header containing `\r\n` (CRLF) characters, resulting in log injection or log forging.
arguments.claim: Logging unvalidated X-Forwarded-For header values directly in ProxyFix debug logs allows log injection/CRLF injection attacks via carriage return and newline characters.

findings.title: Logging unvalidated X-Forwarded-For header values directly in ProxyFix debug logs allows log injection/CRLF injection attacks via carriage return and newline characters.
findings.explanation: The new debug logging statement in ProxyFix logs the value of `x_for` (derived from the `X-Forwarded-For` HTTP header via `_get_real_value` and `parse_list_header`) directly using standard logging (`_logger.debug`). Since `parse_list_header` does not strip newline or carriage return characters from header values, an attacker can supply an `X-Forwarded-For` header containing `\r\n` (CRLF) characters, resulting in log injection or log forging.
findings.suggested_fix: Sanitize `x_for` (e.g. by stripping or replacing newline characters) or log it safely (or via representation/quoting) before passing it to `_logger.debug`.
